My family has farmed this same land in Quzhou for three generations. I have about 6 mu. My knees are not what they were, so I hire the village machine cooperative for the big work — plowing, seeding, harvesting. That is just how it is done now.

I will do what I have always done: wheat in winter, maize in summer, same plot. I never change this. The soil knows these two crops. My father grew them, I grew them, my son grew them before he moved to the city. Switching to vegetables or fruit trees — I hear younger people talk about it, but I am 67. I am not starting over.

For wheat, I will use the improved seed the township station sells — I stopped saving my own seed maybe fifteen years ago when the yields got worse. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then urea at green-up in February. I irrigate three times: before sowing to wet the seedbed, once at jointing, once at heading. I spray herbicide in spring and once more for aphids before heading. Rotary tillage before sowing — the combine leaves stubble and I need it turned under.

For maize, I direct-seed into the stubble right after wheat harvest — no tillage, no time to waste, the season is short. I use hybrid seed,郑单958 or whatever the co-op has. One irrigation if July is dry. One pesticide pass for corn borer. The rains usually help.

I do not measure things carefully. I go by what I buy and what I have always applied. My yield is around 450 for wheat, maybe 550 for maize on a good year.
